transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here. As we all know, Riverside Urgent Care Clinic has requested an emergency blood-product reserve that would be stored on-site at their facility and replenished through our hospital blood bank. This is a significant request, and before I make my final decision on whether this reserve can go live and under what operating requirements, I want to walk through the plan with all of you — transfusion medicine, laboratory operations, courier services, and nursing education. Let's start by hearing from each of you on feasibility, logistics, and any concerns you see. Who would like to begin?

The unit was validated for storage at exactly 2 to 6 degrees Celsius, which meets the temperature requirement for red-cell storage. However, there's a critical prerequisite: our laboratory acceptance record requires a documented temperature-alarm test before any units can be stocked there. That alarm test has not been documented yet, so from my end, that would need to be completed and on file before we can assign any inventory to Riverside — including the 4 O-negative and 2 O-positive units Dr. Alvarez just mentioned.
